title: Graham Crackers
summary: Thin, snappy wholemeal crackers spiced with cinnamon and sweetened with honey, baked until crisp.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
ruler and sharp knife or pizza wheel

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Combine the dry ingredients
steps.text: Pulse the wholemeal flour, plain flour, sugar, cinnamon, salt, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda together in a food processor, or whisk them in a large bowl. Mixing the leaveners evenly through the flour now means they'll act consistently across the whole batch rather than leaving pockets of rise. Add the cold, cubed butter and pulse until the mixture looks like fine crumbs.

steps.title: Add the wet ingredients
steps.text: Add the honey, milk and vanilla, then pulse or mix until the dough starts to clump together. Using cold butter right up to this point keeps tiny flecks of fat intact in the dough, which is part of what gives these crackers their crisp, flaky snap rather than a soft texture. Stop as soon as the dough comes together — it doesn't need to look perfectly smooth.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Press the dough into two flat rectangles, wrap, and chill for 1 hour. Chilling firms the butter back up and relaxes the dough, making it far easier to roll out thinly without it springing back or tearing. This rest also lets the wholemeal flour fully hydrate.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Put a shelf in the middle of the oven and heat it to 175°C (155°C fan), allowing at least 20 minutes. Line two large metal trays with baking paper while the oven comes up to temperature. A fully heated oven helps the thin dough crisp quickly rather than drying out slowly.

steps.title: Roll and score
steps.text: Roll each piece of dough between sheets of baking paper to about 3 mm thick, into a rectangle roughly 20 x 28 cm, then slide it, still on its bottom sheet, onto a tray. Trim the edges, score the dough into 7 x 6 cm rectangles without cutting all the way through, then prick all over with a fork and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar. Rolling the dough thin and even is what makes these crackers snap cleanly rather than bend, and the fork pricks let steam escape so the dough doesn't bubble up unevenly.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake for 14-18 minutes, rotating the trays halfway through, until the crackers are golden brown and firm at the edges. Rotating halfway compensates for any hot spots in the oven, so every cracker browns at roughly the same rate. The edges should feel properly firm, not just coloured, before you take them out.

steps.title: Re-cut and cool
steps.text: While the crackers are still warm, cut back along the scored lines so they separate cleanly, then leave them on the tray for 10 minutes. Cutting warm dough along the scores works far more easily than trying to snap a fully cooled sheet apart. Transfer to a wire rack, where they'll crisp up fully as they finish cooling — the thin, even rolling is really what gives them their final snap.

tips: Keep the butter cold right up until it's pulsed into the flour — warm butter blends in too smoothly and the crackers lose their flaky snap.
Roll the dough as evenly as you can; thick patches stay soft in the middle while thin ones at the edges can scorch.
Cut along the scored lines while the sheet is still warm — a common mistake is waiting until it's cold, when the whole sheet can crack unevenly instead of separating neatly.
Prick the dough well with a fork before baking to stop it puffing up in uneven bubbles.
Rotate the trays halfway through baking, since ovens often have hot spots that brown one side faster than the other.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. They freeze well for up to 2 months; recrisp briefly in a low oven after thawing if needed.
